newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Five soldiers killed in attack in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Five soldiers killed in attack in Burundi.

text.p: Five Burundian soldiers were killed by gunmen who attacked them in the northwestern province of Cibitoke, an army spokesman said on Saturday.
The spokesman said the troops were hunting for Hutu former Rwandan troops and Interahamwe militiamen who had crossed from southern Rwanda into Cibitoke, one of Burundi's most dangerous provinces.
He said the soldiers were killed on Thursday in Mugina commune but gave no details.

Both the Tutsi-dominated Burundian army and Hutu rebels are accused by human rights groups of massacring civilians in reprisal raids after attacks. The army says any troops involved in such killings acted against orders and would be punished.
The U.N. refugee agency said on Thursday a military court convicted 10 Burundian soldiers of involvement in the killing of 122 Burundian refugees after they were expelled from Tanzania in January.
The soldiers were sentenced to jail terms ranging from 10 years to five months. Two others were acquitted, it said.
The army spokesman said on Wednesday 57 civilians died in crossfire during a clash between troops and Hutu rebels at Rumonge south of the capital Bujumbura the previous Thursday.
More than 100,000 people have been killed since 1993 in massacres and civil war between minority Tutsis and majority Hutus.
